name: Iwan
pronunciation: ee-VAHN, Persian for a vaulted hall open on one side
about: Iwan moves from sunlit yellow into a long run of blues drawn from the tiled entrance iwan of Isfahan's Shah Mosque. Ochre and pale blue form a short threshold before turquoise, lapis, cobalt, ultramarine, indigo and midnight blue take over. I made it for maps that need a clear light-to-dark sequence with most of the visual weight carried by blue.
story: An iwan, or ایوان in Persian, is a vaulted space that opens on one side to a courtyard. The form developed in pre-Islamic Iran and became closely tied to Persian architecture. In a four-iwan mosque, one rises from the center of each side of the courtyard. [Smarthistory's guide to mosque architecture](https://smarthistory.org/common-types-of-mosque-architecture/) follows this form from its Iranian roots into later Islamic buildings.

The Shah Mosque stands on the south side of Naqsh-e Jahan Square and was built for Shah Abbas I in the early seventeenth century. Its entrance faces the square, while the prayer hall turns toward Mecca. A passage through the entrance iwan handles that change in direction. [UNESCO's Meidan Emam record](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/115/) describes the deep portal, its tiled half-dome and the angled route into the courtyard.

The blue surface is not a single blue. Turquoise, lapis, white, green and yellow meet in floral scrolls, calligraphy and the small cells of the muqarnas vault. Safavid builders used haft-rangi, or seven-color tilework, to paint several colors on one tile before firing it. [Smarthistory's introduction to Safavid art](https://smarthistory.org/safavids-intro/) explains how this method gave the Shah Mosque its layered, light-catching color. I kept the yellow at one end of the palette, then let the many blues carry the rest of the ramp.
notes: tile yellow, the curling floral vines in the upper panel
golden ochre, shaded yellow leaves and outlines
pale blue, weathered tile and floral highlights
turquoise, bright glazed ribs around the lower vault
lapis blue, the broad floral tile ground
cobalt, darker outlines around the upper arabesques
ultramarine, the most saturated blue tiles
indigo, shadowed geometry in the central muqarnas
midnight blue, the deepest recess of the half-dome
